amarillo.line: Well, we crossed the panhandle and then we headed towards Amarillo
stanza: Well, we crossed the panhandle and then we headed towards Amarillo
We pulled up where Henry Porter used to live. He owned a Wreckin’ lot outside o…
Ruby was in the backyard hanging clothes, she had her red hair tied back. She s…
She said, “Henry ain’t here but you can come on in, he’ll be back in a little w…

amarillo.line: Well, when the wind don't blow in Amarillo
stanza: Well, when the wind don't blow in Amarillo
And the moon along the Gunnison don't rise
Shall I cast my dreams upon your love, babe?
And lie beneath the laughter of your eyes

pillow.line: And woven on the edging of my pillow
stanza: Now the dress is hung, the ticket pawned
The factor max that proved the fact is melted down
And woven on the edging of my pillow
And my brother lays upon the rocks
He could be dead, he could be not, he could be you
He's chameleon, comedian, Corinthian and caricature
Shooting up pie-in-the-sky
The Bewlay Brothers
In the feeble and the bad
The Bewlay Brothers

pillow.line: And I slept on the strange pillows
stanza: I pulled into the Cactus Tree Motel
To shower off the dust
And I slept on the strange pillows
Of my wanderlust
I dreamed of 747s
Over geometric farms

pillow.line: I never give you my pillow
stanza: I never give you my pillow
I only send you my invitations
And in the middle of the celebrations
I break down
I heard somebody call your name
From underneath our willow
I saw something tucked in shame
Underneath your pillow
Well, I've tried so hard, baby
But I just can't see
What a woman like you
Is doing with me

pillow.songTitle: Pagan Angel and a Borrowed Car
pillow.line: Every evening I would watch her hold the pillow
stanza: Love was a promise made of smoke
In a frozen copse of trees
A bone cold and older than our bodies
Slowly floating in the sea
Every morning there were planes
The shiny blades of pagan angels in our father's skies
Every evening I would watch her hold the pillow
Tight against her hollows, her unholy child
I was still a beggar shaking out my stolen coat
Among the angry cemetery leaves
When they caught the king beneath the borrowed car
Righteous, drunk, and fumbling for the royal keys
